source_text: ἰχνευτικῶς, οὕτω δὲ τολμηροὶ καὶ προπετεῖς ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὥστε μόνοι τοὺς Σικιμίτας ἀπέσφαζον ἐθνηδόν.
thought_title: The boldness of Simeon and Levi in slaughtering the Shechemites
orientation: Eustathius is contrasting Joseph's self-control with the murderous boldness of his brothers Simeon and Levi, who slaughtered the Shechemites.
pass_a_gloss: In a tracking manner, and so bold and reckless were the men that alone they were slaughtering the Shechemites nation by nation.

lemmas.gloss: in a tracking manner, like hunters on a scent
nation by nation, by whole peoples

choices.why: Preserves the adverbial force and the hunting imagery of following a scent, which connects to the previous sentence's 'savory smells'.
Captures the headlong, rash quality of their violence, distinct from mere boldness.
The imperfect tense conveys ongoing or repeated action, matching the habitual violence described in the previous sentence.
The rare adverb emphasizes the scale and totality of the killing, treating whole peoples as units of slaughter.

bible_refs.note: Simeon and Levi slaughtering the Shechemites

pass_b_english: They were such bold and reckless men that, like hunters on a scent, they slaughtered the Shechemites by themselves, nation by nation (Genesis 34:25-26).

problems.why: μόνοι means 'alone' (only Simeon and Levi), not 'by themselves'; ἐθνηδόν means 'like a nation/people' (collectively), not 'nation by nation'.
problems.fix: all alone, like a nation unto themselves

edits.old: they slaughtered the Shechemites by themselves, nation by nation
edits.new: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, like a nation unto themselves

problems.why: ἐθνηδόν means 'nation by nation' or 'tribe by tribe' (slaughtering them group by group), not 'like a nation unto themselves'.
problems.fix: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, tribe by tribe (Genesis 34:25).

edits.old: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, like a nation unto themselves (Genesis 34:25).
edits.new: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, tribe by tribe (Genesis 34:25).

problems.why: Genesis 34:25 says Simeon and Levi killed males, not 'tribe by tribe' slaughter.
problems.fix: Cite Genesis 34:25-26 or note hyperbolic expansion.

problems.why: Simeon and Levi acted alone, not tribe by tribe; likely mistranslation of a phrase meaning 'by themselves.'
problems.fix: Render as 'by themselves' or 'on their own.'

edits.old: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, tribe by tribe (Genesis 34:25).
edits.new: they slaughtered the Shechemites all alone, nation by nation (Genesis 34:25-26).

fixed: The scripture citation was updated to Genesis 34:25-26 to reflect the broader slaughter context.
The phrase 'tribe by tribe' was corrected to 'nation by nation' to match the source's 'ἐθνηδόν'.

problems.fix: Emend to 'by themselves' meaning without Jacob's approval, or 'alone' as 'single-handedly'.

problems.why: Cited verses mention swords and killing, but 'nation by nation' and 'all alone' do not match Genesis 34.
problems.fix: Note that citation covers the slaughter, though author's phrasing paraphrases freely.

fixed: The scripture citation Genesis 34:25-26 is appropriate for the slaughter of the Shechemites, even though the author's phrasing paraphrases freely.

last_rejected.why: ἐθνηδόν means 'after the manner of nations/tribes' or 'like gentiles,' not 'tribe by tribe.'
last_rejected.ruling: ἐθνηδόν (ethnēdon) is adverbial from ἔθνος; 'tribe by tribe' captures distributive slaughter by kinship groups, standard rendering.

last_rejected.why: ἰχνευτικῶς means 'trackingly/investigatively,' not 'like hunters on a scent.'
last_rejected.fix: They tracked them down so boldly and recklessly that they alone slaughtered the Shechemites, tribe by tribe.
last_rejected.ruling: ἰχνευτικῶς derives from ἰχνεύω (track/follow scent); 'hunters on a scent' is valid figurative rendering.

last_rejected.why: μόνοι modifies the brothers (they alone did it), not 'all alone' as manner.
last_rejected.fix: they alone slaughtered the Shechemites, tribe by tribe
last_rejected.ruling: μόνοι naturally reads 'they alone slaughtered'; 'all alone' conveys same meaning adequately.

last_rejected.why: The source cites no scripture reference; this is an editorial addition.
last_rejected.ruling: Scripture references are standard editorial aids; not a translation error of source meaning.
